\">\u003cfigcaption>Figure · page 1\u003c/figcaption>\u003c/figure>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">DETAILED MANAGEMENT OF HEART FAILURE\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">KCMC/Tanzania practical approach + AHA/ACC/HFSA + ESC comparison\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">1. First, define and classify the patient\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Heart failure is a clinical syndrome where the heart fails to pump enough blood to meet body\u003cbr>needs, or can do so only with raised filling pressures. It presents with dyspnea, orthopnea,\u003cbr>PND, fatigue, edema, raised JVP, pulmonary congestion, pleural effusion, ascites, or shock.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Before management, classify the patient properly:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">A. By EF\u003c/p>\u003cdiv class=\"table-scroll\">\u003ctable class=\"clinical-table\">\u003ctr>\u003ctd>Type\u003c/td>\u003ctd>EF\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Meaning\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>HFrEF\u003c/td>\u003ctd>≤40%\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Heart failure with reduced EF\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>HFmrEF\u003c/td>\u003ctd>41–49%\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Mildly reduced EF\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>HFpEF\u003c/td>\u003ctd>≥50%\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Preserved EF but raised filling pressures\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>HFimpEF\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Previous EF ≤40%, now &gt;40%\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Improved EF after treatment\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003c/table>\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">This matters because HFrEF has the strongest mortality-reducing drug evidence.\u003cbr>AHA/ACC/HFSA states that guideline-directed medical therapy for HFrEF includes four major\u003cbr>drug classes.\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 2\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">B. By NYHA class\u003c/p>\u003cdiv class=\"table-scroll\">\u003ctable class=\"clinical-table\">\u003ctr>\u003ctd>NYHA\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Functional status\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>I\u003c/td>\u003ctd>No limitation\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>II\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Symptoms with ordinary activity\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>III\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Symptoms with less-than-ordinary activity\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>IV\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Symptoms at rest\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003c/table>\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Always include NYHA in diagnosis.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Example:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">“Acute decompensated congestive heart failure NYHA IV secondary to hypertensive heart  disease.”\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">C. By ACC/AHA stage\u003c/p>\u003cdiv class=\"table-scroll\">\u003ctable class=\"clinical-table\">\u003ctr>\u003ctd>Stage\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Meaning\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>A\u003c/td>\u003ctd>At risk, no structural disease\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>B\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Structural heart disease, no symptoms\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>C\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Structural disease with current/past symptoms\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>D\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Advanced HF, refractory/recurrent symptoms\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003c/table>\u003c/div>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 3\u003c/div>\u003cfigure class=\"note-figure\">\u003cimg loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Illustration associated with page 3\" src=\"data:image/webp;base64,\">\u003cfigcaption>Figure · page 3\u003c/figcaption>\u003c/figure>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">D. By acute hemodynamic profile\u003c/p>\u003cdiv class=\"table-scroll\">\u003ctable class=\"clinical-table\">\u003ctr>\u003ctd>Profile\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Meaning\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Management direction\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>Warm-wet\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Perfused but congested\u003c/td>\u003ctd>IV diuretics ± nitrates\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>Cold-wet\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Hypoperfused and congested\u003c/td>\u003ctd>ICU, vasopressor/inotrope, cautious diuresis\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>Cold-dry\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Hypoperfused but underfilled\u003c/td>\u003ctd>cautious fluid challenge ± inotrope\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>Warm-dry\u003c/td>\u003ctd>compensated\u003c/td>\u003ctd>optimize chronic therapy\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003c/table>\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">This is critical in ward rounds. Do not give furosemide or fluids blindly.\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 4\u003c/div>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">2. General goals of management\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Management aims to:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">1. Relieve congestion and dyspnea.\u003cbr>2. Improve perfusion if shocked.\u003cbr>3. Treat precipitating causes.\u003cbr>4. Reduce mortality and hospitalization.\u003cbr>5. Prevent progression/remodeling.\u003cbr>6. Prevent complications: AKI, arrhythmia, thromboembolism, electrolyte problems.\u003cbr>7. Educate patient and prevent readmission.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">3. Initial management of acute decompensated heart failure\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Step 1: ABCDE assessment\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">A — Airway\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Assess whether the patient can protect airway.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Call ICU/anesthesia early if:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>reduced GCS,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>severe respiratory distress,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>exhaustion,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>aspiration risk,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>severe pulmonary edema not improving.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">B — Breathing\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Sit patient upright.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Give oxygen only if hypoxic.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Targets:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  most patients: SpO₂ ≥92%   •  COPD/CO₂ retainer: SpO₂ 88–92%\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Use CPAP/NIV if:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>acute pulmonary edema,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>severe respiratory distress,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>hypoxia despite oxygen,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>acidosis/hypercapnia,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>patient conscious and cooperative.\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 5\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">NICE recommends considering NIV without delay in acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema with\u003cbr>severe dyspnea and acidaemia or failure to respond to treatment.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">C — Circulation\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Do:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>two IV lines,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>ECG monitor,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>BP/MAP monitoring,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>check pulse rhythm,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>assess JVP,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>assess peripheral perfusion,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>Foley catheter if severe,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>strict input/output chart.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">D — Disability\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Check:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  GCS,   •  RBG,   •  confusion,   •  stroke signs,   •  hypoperfusion.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">E — Exposure\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Look for:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>fever/infection,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>anemia,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>edema,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>DVT,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>ascites,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>medication bottles,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>NSAID/herbal use,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>thyroid signs,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>alcohol use.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">4. Investigations in acute HF\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Do not delay emergency treatment, but investigate early.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Bedside\u003c/h4>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 6\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  SpO₂   •  BP, pulse, RR, temperature   •  RBG   •  ECG   •  urine output\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Blood tests\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>FBP\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>urea/creatinine/eGFR\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>sodium, potassium, bicarbonate\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>magnesium\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>LFTs/albumin\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>troponin if ACS suspected\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>BNP/NT-proBNP if diagnosis uncertain\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>CRP/blood cultures if infection suspected\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>TSH if unexplained HF/AF/thyroid features\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>HbA1c/lipid profile after stabilization\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Imaging\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>CXR\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>echocardiography\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>Doppler/CTPA if PE suspected\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>renal ultrasound if AKI/CKD or obstruction suspected\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Echocardiography must answer\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>EF\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>LV size\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>global vs regional hypokinesia\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>RV function\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>pulmonary pressure\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>valves: MR, TR, AS, AR, MS\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>pericardial effusion\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>thrombus\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>diastolic function\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">5. Identify and treat precipitating factors\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Use FAILURE.\u003c/p>\u003cdiv class=\"table-scroll\">\u003ctable class=\"clinical-table\">\u003ctr>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Letter\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Trigger\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>F\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Forgotten drugs / poor adherence\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>A\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Arrhythmia, especially AF\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>I\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Ischemia or infection\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003c/table>\u003c/div>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 7\u003c/div>\u003cdiv class=\"table-scroll\">\u003ctable class=\"clinical-table\">\u003ctr>\u003ctd>L\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Lifestyle: salt/fluid excess, alcohol, NSAIDs\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>U\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Uncontrolled hypertension\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>R\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Renal failure, pulmonary embolism\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003ctr>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>E\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003ctd>Endocrine/anemia: thyroid disease, severe anemia\u003c/td>\u003ctd>\u003c/td>\u003c/tr>\u003c/table>\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">In KCMC/Tanzania, common triggers are poor adherence, uncontrolled hypertension,\u003cbr>infection, anemia, renal failure, NSAIDs, excess salt/fluid, AF, ACS, PE, and late\u003cbr>presentation.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">6. Management according to acute profile\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">A. Warm-wet heart failure\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">This is the commonest admitted HF patient: congested but perfused.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Features:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>dyspnea,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>orthopnea,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>raised JVP,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>crackles,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>edema,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>ascites,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>pleural effusion,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>BP acceptable,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>warm peripheries.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Treatment\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Give IV loop diuretic.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">KCMC/Tanzania practical regimen:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>Furosemide 40 mg IV stat if diuretic-naïve or mild-moderate congestion.\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>Furosemide 40–80 mg IV stat if severe congestion, CKD, pulmonary edema, or already\u003cbr>on oral furosemide.\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>If already on oral furosemide, IV starting dose should be at least equal to or higher than\u003cbr>total daily oral dose.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">NICE recommends IV diuretic therapy for acute heart failure, using either bolus or infusion  strategy.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Monitor response\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Panel answer:\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 8\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>urine output,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>daily weight,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>fluid balance,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>dyspnea/orthopnea,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>oxygen requirement,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>crackles,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>JVP,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>edema,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>BP,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>creatinine/eGFR,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>sodium,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>potassium,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>magnesium.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Signs patient has decongested\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>can lie flatter,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>reduced orthopnea/PND,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>reduced crackles,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>reduced JVP,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>edema improving,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>weight loss,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>negative fluid balance,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>improved oxygenation,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>improved hepatomegaly/ascites,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>urine output improves.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">B. Hypertensive acute pulmonary edema\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Features:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  severe dyspnea,   •  high BP,   •  pulmonary edema,   •  often preserved perfusion,   •  sympathetic surge.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Treatment\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">1. Sit upright.\u003cbr>2. Oxygen if hypoxic.\u003cbr>3. CPAP/NIV if severe.\u003cbr>4. IV furosemide if congested.\u003cbr>5. Add nitrate if SBP allows.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">If SBP &gt;110 mmHg:\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 9\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  sublingual GTN while preparing infusion, or   •  IV nitroglycerin infusion if available.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Avoid nitrates in:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  hypotension,   •  severe aortic stenosis,   •  RV infarction,   •  recent sildenafil/tadalafil.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">C. Cold-wet heart failure / cardiogenic shock\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">This is dangerous.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Features:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>hypotension or narrow pulse pressure,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>cold extremities,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>altered mentation,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>oliguria,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>delayed capillary refill,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>high lactate/acidosis,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>raised JVP/pulmonary edema/ascites.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Management\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">1. Admit MICU/HDU.\u003cbr>2. Cardiac monitor.\u003cbr>3. Oxygen/NIV/intubation if needed.\u003cbr>4. Avoid large blind fluids.\u003cbr>5. Start vasopressor if hypotensive.\u003cbr>6. Add inotrope if low cardiac output.\u003cbr>7. Cautious diuresis after perfusion support if congested.\u003cbr>8. Urgent echo and ECG.\u003cbr>9. Treat cause: ACS, arrhythmia, PE, infection, valve lesion.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Drugs\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Noradrenaline infusion\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  Start around 0.05–0.1 mcg/kg/min   •  Titrate to MAP/perfusion, commonly MAP ≥65 mmHg.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Dobutamine infusion\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  Start 2.5–5 mcg/kg/min\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 10\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  Titrate according to BP, urine output, perfusion, lactate, rhythm.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Use noradrenaline for pressure and dobutamine for pump contractility.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Hold chronic HF drugs during shock\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Hold/reassess:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  beta-blocker,   •  ACEi/ARB/ARNI,   •  spironolactone/eplerenone,   •  SGLT2 inhibitor,   •  metformin,   •  NSAIDs.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Restart gradually once stable.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">D. Cold-dry profile\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Features:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>cold peripheries,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>low BP/low output,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>no crackles,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>low JVP,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>no edema,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>possible overdiuresis/dehydration.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Treatment\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Give cautious fluid challenge:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  250 mL normal saline or Ringer’s lactate   •  reassess BP, JVP, lungs, urine output, IVC/echo.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">If no response, stop fluids and use inotrope/vasopressor depending findings.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">7. Chronic HFrEF management — four pillars\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">For HFrEF EF ≤40%, use four foundational classes if tolerated:\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">1. ARNI/ACEi/ARB   2. Evidence-based beta-blocker   3. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist   4. SGLT2 inhibitor\u003c/h3>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 11\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">AHA/ACC/HFSA identifies these as the main GDMT classes for HFrEF.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Pillar 1: ARNI / ACE inhibitor / ARB\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Best international option\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Sacubitril/valsartan is preferred over ACEi/ARB in suitable symptomatic HFrEF patients.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">KCMC/Tanzania practical alternatives\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">If ARNI unavailable/costly, use ACEi or ARB.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Enalapril\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  Start 2.5–5 mg PO OD/BD   •  Titrate upward as tolerated.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Losartan\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  Start 25–50 mg PO OD   •  Titrate to 100 mg OD if tolerated.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Benefits\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  reduces mortality,   •  reduces hospitalization,   •  reduces remodeling,   •  reduces afterload.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Avoid/hold if\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>pregnancy,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>bilateral renal artery stenosis,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>angioedema history for ACEi,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>severe hypotension,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>AKI,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>K⁺ ≥5.5 mmol/L,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>rapidly rising creatinine.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Monitoring\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Check creatinine and potassium after starting or increasing dose.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Pillar 2: Evidence-based beta-blocker\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Start only when stable and euvolemic.\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 12\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Options:\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Carvedilol\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  Start 3.125 mg PO BD   •  Titrate slowly.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Bisoprolol\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  Start 1.25 mg PO OD   •  Titrate slowly.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Metoprolol succinate\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  Start 12.5–25 mg PO OD, if available.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Benefits\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>reduces mortality,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>reduces sudden cardiac death,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>reduces remodeling,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>improves EF over time,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>controls sympathetic overactivity.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Do not start/up-titrate if\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>acute pulmonary edema,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>cardiogenic shock,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>severe bradycardia,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>heart block,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>severe hypotension,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>active bronchospasm.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Exam point\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">If asked: “Will you give beta blocker in ADHF?”\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Answer:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">“If patient is in shock, severe hypotension, bradycardia or acute pulmonary edema, I will hold or\u003cbr>avoid starting beta-blocker. If already taking it and decompensation is mild with stable BP and\u003cbr>no shock, I may continue cautiously. I start or uptitrate only after euvolemic and stable.”\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Pillar 3: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Spironolactone\u003c/h4>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 13\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  Start 12.5–25 mg PO OD   •  Titrate if tolerated.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Alternative:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  Eplerenone if gynecomastia or intolerance and available.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Mechanism\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Blocks aldosterone receptor → reduces sodium/water retention, potassium wasting, myocardial  fibrosis and remodeling.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Benefits\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  reduces mortality,   •  reduces HF hospitalization,   •  helps resistant congestion.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Side effects\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>hyperkalemia,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>worsening renal function,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>gynecomastia,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>breast tenderness,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>menstrual irregularities.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Avoid/hold if\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  K⁺ ≥5.0–5.5 mmol/L,   •  severe renal impairment,   •  AKI,   •  hypotension/shock.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Pillar 4: SGLT2 inhibitor\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Options:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Dapagliflozin 10 mg PO OD\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">or\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Empagliflozin 10 mg PO OD\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Benefits\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  reduces HF hospitalization,\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 14\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  improves HF outcomes,   •  renal protection,   •  works even without diabetes in HFrEF.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">ESC 2023 focused update strengthened SGLT2 inhibitor use in HFmrEF and HFpEF to reduce\u003cbr>HF hospitalization and cardiovascular death.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Hold if\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>AKI,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>shock,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>dehydration,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>fasting/perioperative state,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>DKA/suspected DKA,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>severe acute illness.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">8. Diuretics in chronic HF\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Diuretics relieve congestion but are not the main mortality-reducing therapy.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Furosemide\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Practical dose:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  20–40 mg PO OD for mild congestion.   •  40–80 mg PO/IV or higher if severe/CKD.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Adjust to maintain euvolemia.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Monitor\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  weight,   •  urine output,   •  BP,   •  creatinine,   •  sodium,   •  potassium,   •  magnesium,   •  symptoms.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Diuretic resistance\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Think of:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  CKD,   •  high salt intake,\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 15\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  NSAID use,   •  poor gut absorption,   •  low renal perfusion,   •  venous congestion,   •  low albumin.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Management:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>increase loop dose,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>switch to IV,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>consider infusion,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>add thiazide-type diuretic if available,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>consider dialysis/ultrafiltration if refractory overload.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Loop diuretics remain first-line for decongestion in congestive HF.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">9. Management of HFmrEF and HFpEF\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">HFmrEF EF 41–49%\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Treat similarly to HFrEF when EF is near 40, especially if previous reduced EF.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Use:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>diuretics for congestion,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>SGLT2 inhibitor,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>ACEi/ARB/ARNI in selected patients,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>beta-blocker if ischemic disease, AF, previous HFrEF,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>MRA in selected patients.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">HFpEF EF ≥50%\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Focus on:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">1. Diuretics for congestion.\u003cbr>2. BP control.\u003cbr>3. Treat AF.\u003cbr>4. Treat ischemia.\u003cbr>5. Treat obesity, DM, CKD, OSA.\u003cbr>6. SGLT2 inhibitor if eligible.\u003cbr>7. Manage pulmonary hypertension/valvular disease if present.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">HFpEF is not “normal heart failure.” The EF is preserved, but filling pressure is high.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">10. Management of right-sided HF / cor pulmonale\u003c/h3>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 16\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Common causes:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  COPD,   •  pulmonary hypertension,   •  ILD,   •  chronic pulmonary TB,   •  PE,   •  left-sided HF,   •  TR.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Management:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>treat underlying lung disease,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>oxygen if hypoxic,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>diuretics for systemic congestion,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>avoid overdiuresis,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>manage pulmonary hypertension cause,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>anticoagulate if PE/DVT,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>manage COPD with bronchodilators, smoking cessation, LTOT if indicated.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Signs:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  raised JVP,   •  hepatomegaly,   •  ascites,   •  peripheral edema,   •  loud P2,   •  TR murmur.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">11. AF management in HF\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">If unstable with hypotension, shock, pulmonary edema, chest pain:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  synchronized DC cardioversion.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">If stable:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>rate control,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>anticoagulation based on CHA₂DS₂-VASc,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>treat trigger,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>consider rhythm control if recent onset/symptomatic/HF worsening.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Drugs:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  beta-blocker if stable HFrEF,   •  digoxin useful in HFrEF with low BP,\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 17\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  amiodarone if rhythm control needed or severe LV dysfunction.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Avoid:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  verapamil/diltiazem in HFrEF due to negative inotropy.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">12. Anticoagulation in HF\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Do not anticoagulate all HF patients automatically.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Indications:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>AF/flutter with stroke risk,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>LV thrombus,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>DVT/PE,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>mechanical valve,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>severe mitral stenosis with AF.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">13. Non-pharmacological management\u003c/h3>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Lifestyle\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>salt restriction,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>fluid restriction if hyponatremia or recurrent congestion,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>daily weight,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>stop smoking,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>stop alcohol,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>avoid NSAIDs,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>exercise/cardiac rehab after stabilization,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>vaccination where available,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>adherence counseling.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Patient counseling in Kiswahili\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">“Punguza chumvi kwenye chakula, epuka dawa za maumivu kama ibuprofen/diclofenac bila\u003cbr>ushauri, tumia dawa zako kila siku, pima uzito mara kwa mara, rudi hospitali ukiona miguu\u003cbr>inavimba zaidi, pumzi inaongezeka, unashindwa kulala chali, au uzito unaongezeka haraka.”\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">14. Device therapy and referral\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Consider cardiology referral for:\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">ICD\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">For selected HFrEF patients with EF ≤35% despite optimized therapy and good expected  survival.\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 18\u003c/div>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">CRT\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">If:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  EF low,   •  wide QRS,   •  especially LBBB,   •  persistent symptoms despite GDMT.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Valve intervention\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">If severe MR, AS, AR, MS, TR contributing to HF.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Coronary evaluation/revascularization\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">If ischemic cardiomyopathy suspected.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Advanced HF referral\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Refer if:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>recurrent admissions,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>EF &lt;25–30%,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>inotrope need,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>refractory congestion,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>cardiorenal syndrome,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>low BP limiting GDMT,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>recurrent arrhythmias,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>cachexia,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>NYHA III–IV despite treatment.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">15. Management of complications\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">A. Cardiorenal syndrome\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Mechanisms:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  low cardiac output,   •  renal venous congestion,   •  RAAS activation,   •  diuretics/poor intake.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Management:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  assess wet/dry and warm/cold,   •  maintain perfusion,\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 19\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>decongest carefully,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>avoid nephrotoxins,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>hold ACEi/ARB/MRA/SGLT2i temporarily if AKI/hyperkalemia/shock,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>dialysis if AEIOU indications.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">B. Hyponatremia\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Usually dilutional due to ADH activation.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Management:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  fluid restriction if severe/recurrent,   •  treat congestion,   •  avoid rapid correction,   •  monitor sodium.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">C. Hyperkalemia\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Common with AKI, ACEi/ARB/MRA.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">If ECG changes/severe:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>calcium gluconate,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>insulin-dextrose,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>salbutamol,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>bicarbonate if acidotic,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>dialysis if refractory.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">D. Pleural effusion/ascites\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Usually transudative from congestion.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Management:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  treat HF with diuretics,   •  tap if unilateral, febrile, very large, atypical, or not responding.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">16. Monitoring inpatient HF\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Daily:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  symptoms,   •  BP/HR/RR/SpO₂,   •  JVP,   •  edema,   •  chest crackles,\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 20\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>weight,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>input/output,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>urine output,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>creatinine/eGFR,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>sodium/potassium,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>oxygen requirement,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>ECG rhythm if unstable.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">17. Discharge criteria\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Discharge when:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>clinically stable,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>no worsening dyspnea,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>oxygen stable/off if possible,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>euvolemic or near-euvolemic,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>on oral diuretics,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>renal function/electrolytes stable,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>GDMT started or plan documented,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>patient educated,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>follow-up arranged.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">NICE recommends discharge after acute HF when clinical condition is stable and a management  plan is in place.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">18. Follow-up plan\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Within 1–2 weeks if recently admitted or medication changed:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>symptoms,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>BP/HR,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>weight,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>edema/JVP,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>creatinine,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>potassium,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>sodium,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>adherence,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>titrate GDMT.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Long term:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>optimize four pillars,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>repeat echo after 3–6 months of therapy if HFrEF,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>manage comorbidities,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>vaccination,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>education.\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 21\u003c/div>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">19. Tanzania/KCMC vs international guideline comparison\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">KCMC/Tanzania practical approach\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Common practical management:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>ABCDE,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>oxygen if hypoxic,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>IV furosemide for congestion,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>nitrates if hypertensive pulmonary edema and available,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>noradrenaline + dobutamine for cardiogenic shock,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>enalapril/losartan, carvedilol/bisoprolol, spironolactone, dapagliflozin/empagliflozin\u003cbr>when stable,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>echo-based management,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>treat triggers: infection, anemia, AF, ACS, PE, renal failure,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>dialysis if refractory overload/AKI complications.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">AHA/ACC/HFSA / ESC approach\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">International approach emphasizes:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•\u003cbr>early GDMT with four pillars in HFrEF,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>ARNI preferred where possible,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>SGLT2 inhibitors across HFrEF and now strongly in HFmrEF/HFpEF,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>IV iron in selected iron-deficient HF patients,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>ICD/CRT when indicated,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>advanced HF referral,\u003cbr>•\u003cbr>mechanical circulatory support/transplant in selected stage D HF.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">The major difference is availability and cost of ARNI, device therapy, cardiac MRI, coronary\u003cbr>intervention, transplant/LVAD, and specialized HF clinics.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">20. Practical prescription-style examples\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Stable HFrEF outpatient example\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">If BP, renal function and K⁺ allow:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">1. Enalapril 2.5 mg PO BD or Losartan 50 mg OD\u003cbr>2. Carvedilol 3.125 mg PO BD when euvolemic\u003cbr>3. Spironolactone 25 mg PO OD if K⁺ acceptable\u003cbr>4. Dapagliflozin 10 mg PO OD\u003cbr>5. Furosemide 40 mg PO OD if congested\u003cbr>6. Atorvastatin if ASCVD/diabetes/high risk\u003cbr>7. Salt restriction, daily weight, follow-up labs.\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 22\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Acute congested HF admission example\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">1. Sit upright.\u003cbr>2. Oxygen if hypoxic.\u003cbr>3. ECG, CXR, FBP, U&amp;E/Cr, K⁺/Na⁺, troponin if indicated.\u003cbr>4. Foley if severe.\u003cbr>5. Furosemide 40–80 mg IV stat.\u003cbr>6. Monitor urine output and BP.\u003cbr>7. Treat precipitant.\u003cbr>8. Start/restart GDMT once stable.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Cardiogenic shock example\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">1. MICU/HDU.\u003cbr>2. ABCDE, oxygen/NIV/intubation if needed.\u003cbr>3. ECG, urgent echo, lactate, renal/electrolytes.\u003cbr>4. Noradrenaline infusion for MAP/perfusion.\u003cbr>5. Dobutamine infusion if poor contractility.\u003cbr>6. Avoid blind fluids.\u003cbr>7. Cautious diuresis if congested after perfusion support.\u003cbr>8. Hold beta-blocker/ACEi/MRA/SGLT2i temporarily.\u003cbr>9. Treat ACS/arrhythmia/PE/infection/valve lesion.\u003c/p>\u003ch3 class=\"note-text-block\">21. Common exam questions and answers\u003c/h3>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Q1. How do you know patient has heart failure?\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">“By symptoms and signs of congestion or low output, supported by objective evidence. I would\u003cbr>use history, examination, CXR, ECG, BNP/NT-proBNP if available, and echocardiography.”\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Q2. What is the definitive investigation?\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">“Echocardiography is key because it shows EF, chamber size, valves, wall motion, RV function,\u003cbr>pulmonary pressures, pericardium and thrombus. BNP/NT-proBNP supports diagnosis but does\u003cbr>not replace echo.”\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Q3. What do you monitor after furosemide?\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">“Urine output, weight, fluid balance, BP, dyspnea, JVP, edema, crackles, oxygen requirement,\u003cbr>creatinine, sodium, potassium and magnesium.”\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Q4. Does EF change management?\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">“Yes. HFrEF needs four-pillar mortality-reducing therapy. HFpEF management focuses on\u003cbr>decongestion, BP control, comorbidity management and SGLT2 inhibitor if eligible.”\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 23\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Q5. Will you give beta-blocker in acute HF?\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">“Not if the patient has cardiogenic shock, severe hypotension, bradycardia or acute pulmonary\u003cbr>edema. I start or uptitrate beta-blocker only once stable and euvolemic.”\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Q6. How do you manage HF with AF?\u003c/p>\u00
